# fbfast

> Read-only Firebird 5 client for Python (CPython 3.11-3.15) with a Rust core
> and the official Firebird client bundled in the wheel. One API, sync and
> asyncio, returns tuples, dicts, validated Pydantic models, native JSON bytes,
> pyarrow Tables or Polars DataFrames, materialized or streamed.

Key rules: only single SELECT/WITH statements in READ ONLY transactions (not a
sandbox: use a minimal database role); positional `?` parameters whose Python
type matches the SQL type; methods without a suffix block and `_async` methods
(plus `aclose`) are coroutines; always use context managers for pools,
snapshots, streams and query groups; UTF8 connections only; one operation at a
time per snapshot or stream; create pools after `fork()`. Reach a named pool
with `fbfast.get_pool(name)`. The installed package carries the same rules
offline in `fbfast/llms.txt`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/README.md): overview, installation, choosing a result type, async services, streams, Arrow/Polars, snapshots
- [Rules for code assistants](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/python/fbfast/llms.txt): hard rules, goal-to-method table, parameter types, defaults, errors and pitfalls in one page
- [Recipes](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/recipes.md): FastAPI with a named pool, NDJSON over HTTP, Polars/Parquet ETL, Arrow streaming, snapshot reports, Pydantic models, concurrent queries
- [Errors](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/errors.md): exception hierarchy, phases, when each error happens and whether retrying helps
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md): wire encryption, roles, charsets, parameter types, slow BLOBs over a WAN, Decimal256 in Polars, timeouts, fork safety
- [Configuration](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/configuration.md): every FirebirdConfig option with its FB_* variable and default
- [Performance](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/performance.md): latency, round trips, BLOBs, compression and when to use each output
- [API reference](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/api.md): signatures and docstrings of the public API

## Examples

# fbfast 0.3.0

> Read-only Firebird 5 client for Python with a Rust core and the official
> Firebird client bundled in the wheel. Returns tuples, dicts, Pydantic models,
> native JSON bytes, pyarrow Tables or Polars DataFrames; sync and asyncio.
> This file ships inside the package for code assistants working offline.

Scope: SELECT/WITH queries against Firebird 5.0.x servers over TCP. No writes,
no DDL, no ORM, no embedded connections. CPython 3.11-3.15 with the GIL on
macOS (arm64, x86_64), Linux glibc (x86_64, aarch64) and Windows x86_64.
Install: `pip install fbfast`; extras `fbfast[pydantic]`, `fbfast[arrow]`, `fbfast[polars]`.

## Hard rules

1. Read-only, but not a sandbox. Only single SELECT/WITH statements run, in
   READ ONLY transactions; selectable procedures can still have side effects.
   Use a database role limited to the tables needed. Never pass SQL from users
   or LLM output; pick from an allowlist and bind values.
2. Parameters are positional `?` placeholders with a list or tuple:
   `pool.fetch_all("... WHERE ID = ? AND STATUS = ?", [10, "OPEN"])`.
   No named parameters, no string formatting of values into SQL.
   Values must match the SQL type exactly (see "Parameter types").
3. Naming: no suffix = blocking; `_async` suffix (and `aclose`) = coroutine.
   `pool.close()` / `await pool.aclose()`, `pool.warmup()` / `await pool.warmup_async()`,
   `init_pool()` / `await init_pool_async()`, `close_pool()` / `await close_pool_async()`.
4. Always use context managers: `with Pool(config) as pool`, `with pool.snapshot() as snap`,
   `with pool.stream(...) as batches`, `with pool.run_many(...) as group`
   (`async with` for the async forms). Otherwise close explicitly in `finally`.
5. Connection charset is UTF8 only (default). Column charsets are converted by the server.
6. One operation at a time per snapshot and per stream; a second raises
   `ConcurrentUseError`. Do not share them between threads or tasks.
7. Create pools after `fork()` (in each worker). Importing before fork is fine.
8. Canonical access to a named pool is `fbfast.get_pool(name).method(...)`.
   Module functions such as `fbfast.fetch_all(sql, pool="name")` are frozen shortcuts.

## Minimal patterns

```python
import fbfast

config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig()            # reads FB_HOST, FB_DATABASE, FB_USER, FB_PASSWORD... and .env
with fbfast.Pool(config) as pool:
    rows = pool.fetch_all("SELECT ID, NAME FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE CITY = ?", ["Recife"])

async with fbfast.Pool(config) as pool:
    row = await pool.fetch_one_async("SELECT ID, NAME FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE ID = ?", [1], as_dict=True)

# Application-wide named pool (e.g. FastAPI lifespan), reached anywhere by name:
await fbfast.init_pool_async(config, name="reports")
total = await fbfast.get_pool("reports").fetch_val_async("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS")
await fbfast.close_pool_async("reports")
```

## Goal -> method (on Pool and Snapshot; each has an `_async` twin)

| Goal | Method | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All rows | `fetch_all(sql, params)` | `list[tuple]` |
| All rows as dicts | `fetch_all(sql, params, as_dict=True)` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` |
| Validated models | `fetch_all(sql, params, model=Order)` | `list[Order]` |
| First row or None | `fetch_one(...)` (same `as_dict=`/`model=`) | `tuple`/`dict`/`Order`/`None` |
| First column of first row | `fetch_val(sql, params)` | value or `None` |
| JSON array built in Rust | `fetch_json(sql, params)` | `bytes` |
| pyarrow.Table | `fetch_arrow(sql, params)` | needs `fbfast[arrow]` |
| polars.DataFrame | `fetch_polars(sql, params, unsupported="error")` | needs `fbfast[polars]` |
| Large result in row batches | `with stream(sql, params, batch_rows=, as_dict=) as b: for rows in b` | `list` per batch |
| NDJSON / JSON chunks | `with stream_json(sql, params, format="ndjson") as c: for chunk in c` | `bytes` per chunk |
| Arrow batches | `with stream_arrow(sql, params) as s: for batch in s` | `ArrowBatch` |
| Execution plan | `explain(sql, params)` | `str` |
| Consistent multi-query read | `with pool.snapshot(timeout=) as snap:` | `Snapshot` (same methods) |
| Several queries at once | `pool.run_all([Query...], concurrency=, timeout=, fail_fast=True)` | `Results`; `results[q]` |
| Results as they finish | `with pool.run_many(queries) as g: for done in g: done.result()` | `Done` |
| Async groups | `await pool.run_all_async(...)`, `async with pool.run_many_async(...) as g: async for done in g` | |
| Pool counters | `pool.stats()` | `PoolStats` |
| Per-query timings | `pool.diagnostics()` with `FirebirdConfig(diagnostics=True)` | `list[QueryTrace]` |
| Negotiated session | `pool.session_info()` | `SessionInfo` or `None` |
| After DDL | `pool.clear_statement_cache()` | |

Async streams: `async with pool.stream_async(...) as b: async for rows in b`
(likewise `stream_json_async`, `stream_arrow_async`). Sync streams close with
`close()`, async ones with `aclose()`.

Query factories for groups: `fbfast.Query.fetch_all / fetch_one / fetch_val /
fetch_json / fetch_arrow / fetch_polars / explain`, same arguments as the pool
methods plus `timeout=`. Each Query object is a distinct key; using the same
object twice raises `ArgumentError`. Groups run only on a Pool, never inside a
snapshot, and each query has its own transaction. `concurrency` defaults to and
is capped at `pool_size`. Group `timeout=` cancels unfinished queries; leaving a
`run_many` block cancels them too. Prefer `run_all_async` to `asyncio.gather`:
gathering more than `pool_size + max_waiters` (264 by default) calls raises `PoolBusyError`.

## Parameter types

`str` for CHAR/VARCHAR; `int` for SMALLINT/INTEGER/BIGINT/INT128;
`decimal.Decimal` or `int` for NUMERIC/DECIMAL (`float` rejected); `float` for
DOUBLE/FLOAT (`int` rejected); `datetime.date` for DATE; `datetime.datetime` for
TIMESTAMP; `datetime.time` for TIME; `bool` for BOOLEAN; `None` for NULL.
Strings are never parsed into dates or numbers. A mismatch raises
`DataConversionError` (phase `bind`).

## Results and types

- Unquoted column names are UPPER CASE (`ID`, `NAME`). Dicts, models, JSON
  records, Arrow and Polars need unique column names: alias duplicates.
- NUMERIC/DECIMAL/INT128 -> exact `Decimal`/`int`; DECFLOAT -> `Decimal`;
  TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE -> aware `datetime`; TIME WITH TIME ZONE ->
  `fbfast.TimeWithZone`; text BLOB -> `str`; binary BLOB -> `bytes`;
  charset NONE text -> `bytes` unless `fallback_charset="UTF8"`.
- CHAR keeps trailing spaces unless `trim_char=True` or `TRIM()` in SQL.
- JSON defaults: exact decimals and BIGINT/INT128 as strings (`json_decimals="string"`,
  `json_integers="safe"`), binary rejected (`json_binary="error"`), NaN/Infinity rejected.
- `model=` needs Pydantic v2; validation runs after fetching (async: in a thread)
  and raises `pydantic.ValidationError`. Streams do not accept `model=`.

## Limits and defaults

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pool_size` / `min_idle` | 8 / 2 | Max connections / kept ready |
| `max_waiters` | 256 | Queue length; full -> `PoolBusyError` |
| `acquire_timeout` | 5.0 s | Wait for a ready connection -> `PoolTimeoutError` |
| `connect_timeout` | 5.0 s | Attach + handshake of one connection |
| `query_timeout` | 30.0 s | Per query incl. fetch, conversion, stream consumption; `timeout=None` disables |
| `snapshot_timeout` | 300.0 s | Whole snapshot scope incl. time between queries |
| `stream_idle_timeout` | 30.0 s | Stream waiting for its consumer |
| `max_result_bytes` | 512 MiB | Per materialized result; not for streams |
| `max_result_rows` | None | Per materialized result |
| `max_blob_bytes` | 64 MiB | Per BLOB value, streams included |
| `fetch_size` / `batch_bytes` | 5000 rows / 4 MiB | Batch targets (also stream `batch_rows` default) |
| `wire_crypt` | "required" | "enabled" allows plaintext; "disabled" refuses encryption |
| `health_check_after` | 30.0 s | Idle ping in the background (keepalive) |
| `ready_transaction_timeout` | 2.0 s | Keep the next query's transaction ready; None disables |

## Configuration

`FirebirdConfig(**options)` precedence: explicit argument > `FB_<NAME>` env var >
`.env` in the current directory > default. Required: `database`, `user`,
`password` (env `FB_DATABASE`, `FB_USER`, `FB_PASSWORD`). Common: `host`
("localhost"), `port` (3050), `role`, `session_time_zone` ("UTC"),
`wire_compression` (False), `fallback_charset`, `trim_char`, `diagnostics`,
`max_inline_blob_size` (client default 65535, 0 disables), `blob_cache_size`,
`env_file` (path or False). `FirebirdConfig.from_env("FB_BI_")` reads another
prefix. Config is immutable; `read_only=False` raises `UnsupportedFeatureError`;
unknown options raise `ConfigurationError`. Construction never connects; `Pool()`
is lazy; entering `with Pool(...)` opens `min_idle` connections and fails fast.

## Errors (all derive from fbfast.FbFastError; attributes phase, sqlstate, native_codes, cleanup_errors)

| Exception | Retry? | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConfigurationError` | no | Bad/missing/unknown option |
| `UnsupportedFeatureError` | no | `read_only=False`, a connection charset other than UTF8 |
| `UnsupportedStatementError` | no | Not a single read-only SELECT/WITH (phase `validate`) |
| `UsageError` (RuntimeError) | no | Snapshot/stream used outside its `with`, entered twice |
| `ArgumentError` (ValueError, TypeError) | no | Invalid argument, bad `model=`, non-Query in run_all |
| `PoolBusyError` | later | Queue full or too many pending async calls |
| `ConcurrentUseError` (PoolBusyError) | no | Snapshot/stream used twice at once |
| `PoolTimeoutError` (TimeoutError) | later | No connection within `acquire_timeout` |
| `PoolClosedError` | no | Pool closed |
| `PoolNotInitializedError` / `PoolAlreadyInitializedError` | no | Named-pool registry misuse |
| `ForkSafetyError` | no | Pool/stream/snapshot used after fork |
| `QueryError` | usually no | Firebird rejected the SQL; see `sqlstate` |
| `QueryTimeoutError` (QueryError, TimeoutError) | longer deadline | Query, snapshot, group or stream-idle deadline |
| `DatabaseConnectionError` (QueryError, ConnectionError) | yes | Attach failed or connection lost (SQLSTATE 08xxx); SQL is never repeated by fbfast |
| `AuthenticationError` | no | Wrong credentials, or wire_crypt mismatch (code 335545064) |
| `RoleNotActiveError` | no | Role missing or not granted |
| `DataConversionError` | no | Parameter type/count, duplicate column names, inexact value |
| `UnsupportedTypeError` | no | ARRAY, or Decimal256 in `fetch_polars` |
| `ResultLimitError` | no | `max_result_bytes`/`max_result_rows`/`max_blob_bytes` exceeded |
| `QueryCancelledError` | depends | Stream closed, group cancelled, pool shut down |
| `CleanupError` | no | Closing failed; connection discarded |

Deferred cleanup: a pooled query replies first; the session reset runs afterwards
and also starts the next query's transaction, so a busy connection answers in
1 round trip (2 after `ready_transaction_timeout`, 2 s, of idleness). A cleanup
failure is counted in `stats()["cleanup_errors"]` and the caller keeps its complete
result. If the link drops within those 2 s, the next query on that connection
raises `DatabaseConnectionError` (SQL already sent is never repeated); later, a
dead connection is replaced transparently. Any error inside a snapshot ends it;
later calls and leaving the block re-raise it.

## Pitfalls

- BLOBs over a WAN: inline BLOBs need server >= 5.0.3 (prefer 5.0.4+). Check
  `pool.session_info()["inline_blobs"]`. UTF8/ISO8859_1/NONE/OCTETS/binary BLOBs
  travel inline up to 65535 bytes; other text charsets (WIN1252...) cost a round
  trip per value. CAST short text to a small VARCHAR.
- Decimal256 in Polars: SUM over BIGINT/NUMERIC(18,x), BIGINT*BIGINT, INT128 and
  NUMERIC(38,x) are INT128-based. `fetch_polars` raises `UnsupportedTypeError`;
  CAST in SQL or pass `unsupported="string"` (exact decimal text).
- Duplicate column names (joins: `O.ID, C.ID`) fail for dicts, models, JSON
  records, Arrow and Polars with `DataConversionError`. Alias them.
- Pydantic fields: name them in UPPER CASE or use `Field(validation_alias="ID")`.
- Snapshot deadline: `snapshot_timeout` (300 s) counts Python time between queries;
  `timeout=None` on a query does not disable it.
- Streams: `query_timeout` covers the whole stream; pass `timeout=` for long
  exports. Keep HTTP stream contexts inside the response generator.
- Wire compression: `wire_compression=True` only requests it; verify
  `session_info()["wire_compressed"]`.
- Upgrading from 0.2: `await pool.close()` is now a TypeError; use `await pool.aclose()`.

# Recipes

Short, complete patterns for common jobs. Every snippet uses the public API of
fbfast 0.3.0; the runnable versions live in
[`examples/`](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/tree/v0.3.0/examples).
Table and column names such as `ORDERS` stand for your own schema.

Conventions used below:

- Methods without a suffix block; methods ending in `_async` (and `aclose`) are
  coroutines.
- Parameters are positional `?` placeholders, passed as a list or tuple.
- Pools, snapshots and streams are always used as context managers, or closed
  explicitly in a `finally`/lifespan.
- `get_pool(name).method(...)` is the canonical way to reach a named pool; the
  module functions such as `fbfast.fetch_all(sql, pool=name)` are shortcuts for it.

## FastAPI with a named pool

Open the pool once in the application lifespan, reach it by name in routes,
and close it on shutdown.

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

import fbfast


class Order(BaseModel):
    id: int = Field(validation_alias="ID")
    customer: str = Field(validation_alias="CUSTOMER")


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # FirebirdConfig() reads FB_* variables (or FB_REPORTS_* with from_env).
    await fbfast.init_pool_async(fbfast.FirebirdConfig(), name="reports")
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        await fbfast.close_pool_async("reports")


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def reports() -> fbfast.Pool:
    return fbfast.get_pool("reports")  # never opens a pool implicitly


@app.get("/orders/count")
async def count_orders(status: str = "OPEN") -> int:
    return await reports().fetch_val_async(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?", [status]
    )


@app.get("/orders/{order_id}")
async def get_order(order_id: int) -> Order | None:
    return await reports().fetch_one_async(
        "SELECT ID, CUSTOMER FROM ORDERS WHERE ID = ?", [order_id], model=Order
    )
```

- `init_pool_async` warms the pool (opens `min_idle` connections) and fails
  fast if the database is unreachable, so a misconfigured service does not start.
- Run one pool per process. With several Uvicorn/Gunicorn workers, the lifespan
  runs in each worker after it was forked, which is what fbfast requires.
- Every `*_async` call runs off the event loop. More concurrent requests than
  `pool_size + max_waiters` raise `PoolBusyError` immediately; map it to HTTP 503.
- Synchronous scripts use the same registry: `fbfast.init_pool(config, name=...)`
  and `fbfast.close_pool(name)`.

## NDJSON streaming over HTTP

`stream_json_async` writes newline-delimited JSON in Rust and yields `bytes`
chunks that always end on a complete record. Keep the stream context **inside**
the response generator, so it opens when the body starts and closes when the
body ends or the client disconnects.

```python
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse


@app.get("/orders.ndjson")
async def export_orders(status: str = "OPEN") -> StreamingResponse:
    async def body():
        async with reports().stream_json_async(
            "SELECT ID, CUSTOMER, TOTAL, CREATED_AT FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?",
            [status],
            timeout=None,  # no total deadline; stream_idle_timeout still applies
        ) as chunks:
            async for chunk in chunks:
                yield chunk

    return StreamingResponse(body(), media_type="application/x-ndjson")
```

- `query_timeout` (30 s by default) covers the whole stream, including the time
  the client takes to read it. Pass `timeout=` for long exports. A consumer that
  stops reading is bounded separately by `stream_idle_timeout`.
- An error after the headers were sent can only terminate the body; it cannot
  become an error status. Validate parameters before returning the response.
- Exact decimals are JSON strings and BIGINT/INT128 are strings by default
  (`json_decimals="string"`, `json_integers="safe"`), so JavaScript clients do
  not lose precision. Pass `"number"` to either option to emit numbers.
- For a single JSON document use `fetch_json_async` (returns `bytes`) and
  `Response(content=..., media_type="application/json")`.

## ETL to Polars and Parquet

`fetch_polars` builds the DataFrame through Arrow without Python rows and
without requiring PyArrow:

```python
from datetime import datetime

import fbfast

with fbfast.Pool(fbfast.FirebirdConfig()) as pool:
    frame = pool.fetch_polars(
        "SELECT ID, CUSTOMER, TOTAL, CREATED_AT FROM ORDERS WHERE CREATED_AT >= ?",
        [datetime(2026, 1, 1)],  # a TIMESTAMP parameter takes a datetime, not a str
    )
    frame.write_parquet("orders.parquet")
```

When the result does not fit comfortably in memory, stream Arrow batches into
the Parquet writer instead (requires `fbfast[arrow]`):

```python
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

with pool.stream_arrow("SELECT ID, CUSTOMER, TOTAL FROM ORDERS", batch_rows=50_000) as stream:
    reader = pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(stream)
    with pq.ParquetWriter("orders.parquet", reader.schema) as writer:
        for batch in reader:
            writer.write_batch(batch)
```

- Install the extras you need: `fbfast[polars]`, `fbfast[arrow]`, or both.
- `SUM()` over `NUMERIC(18, x)` or `BIGINT`, and `BIGINT * BIGINT`, are INT128
  in Firebird 4+, which Arrow represents as Decimal256. Polars cannot hold
  Decimal256, so `fetch_polars` raises `UnsupportedTypeError` unless you
  `CAST(SUM(TOTAL) AS NUMERIC(18, 2))` in SQL or pass `unsupported="string"`
  to receive exact decimal text.
- `max_result_bytes` (512 MiB by default) bounds `fetch_polars`/`fetch_arrow`;
  streams are bounded by `batch_bytes` and `prefetch_batches` instead.

## Arrow streaming

`stream_arrow` yields owned `ArrowBatch` objects. They implement the Arrow C
Data Interface, so PyArrow, Polars and other Arrow consumers can read them
without copying, and they remain valid after the stream closes.

```python
import polars as pl

with pool.stream_arrow("SELECT ID, TOTAL FROM ORDERS", batch_rows=10_000) as batches:
    print(batches.schema.names)  # available right after entering, even for empty results
    for batch in batches:
        frame = pl.DataFrame(batch)  # or pyarrow.record_batch(batch)
        process(frame)
```

The async variant iterates batches; it has no blocking C Stream export:

```python
async with pool.stream_arrow_async("SELECT ID, TOTAL FROM ORDERS") as batches:
    async for batch in batches:
        await process_async(batch)  # ArrowBatch: num_rows, num_columns, nbytes, schema
```

Use either iteration or the C Stream export
(`pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(stream)`) on a given sync stream, not both.

## A report with a snapshot

A snapshot reserves one connection with a READ ONLY SNAPSHOT transaction, so
every query inside sees the same committed data. It is also the fastest way to
run many small sequential queries over a slow link: each costs about one round
trip.

```python
with pool.snapshot(timeout=120.0) as snap:
    totals = snap.fetch_one(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) AS ORDERS, SUM(TOTAL) AS REVENUE FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?",
        ["PAID"], as_dict=True,
    )
    by_customer = snap.fetch_all(
        "SELECT CUSTOMER, SUM(TOTAL) AS REVENUE FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ? "
        "GROUP BY CUSTOMER ORDER BY 2 DESC ROWS 10",
        ["PAID"],
    )
    with snap.stream("SELECT ID, TOTAL FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?", ["PAID"]) as batches:
        for rows in batches:
            write_detail(rows)
```

The same code works asynchronously with `async with pool.snapshot() as snap:`
and the `*_async` methods.

- Only one operation runs at a time inside a snapshot, including an open stream;
  a second one raises `ConcurrentUseError`. Do not share a snapshot between
  threads or tasks; use `run_all` on the pool for parallel work.
- The snapshot deadline (`snapshot_timeout`, 300 s by default, or `timeout=`)
  counts the time your code spends between queries. Each query inside still
  has its own `query_timeout`.
- Any error ends the snapshot: later calls on it, and leaving the `with` block,
  raise that error again. Handle errors outside the block and open a new snapshot.

## Pydantic models

Pass `model=` to `fetch_all`/`fetch_one` (and their async versions, snapshots
and `Query` objects). The return type follows the class: `list[Order]` and
`Order | None`.

```python
from decimal import Decimal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Order(BaseModel):
    id: int = Field(validation_alias="ID")
    customer: str = Field(validation_alias="CUSTOMER")
    total: Decimal = Field(validation_alias="TOTAL")


orders = pool.fetch_all("SELECT ID, CUSTOMER, TOTAL FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?",
                        ["OPEN"], model=Order)
```

- Install with `pip install "fbfast[pydantic]"` (Pydantic v2).
- Firebird returns unquoted names in UPPER CASE (`ID`, `CUSTOMER`). Either name
  the fields that way or map them with `Field(validation_alias=...)`, as above.
  Column names are never renamed silently.
- Every column name must be unique: alias expressions and joined columns
  (`SELECT O.ID, C.ID AS CUSTOMER_ID ...`), or the call raises `DataConversionError`.
- Validation runs after fetching, outside the query deadline; async validation
  runs in a worker thread. A row that fails raises `pydantic.ValidationError`.
- Streams do not accept `model=`; validate each batch yourself
  (`stream(..., as_dict=True)` + `Order.model_validate(row)`).

## Several queries at once

Describe each query with a `fbfast.Query` factory, then run them together.
At most `concurrency` queries hold a connection at once (default and maximum:
`pool_size`); the rest wait outside the pool queue, so other callers keep being
served and there is no limit on the number of queries.

```python
from fbfast import Query

open_orders = Query.fetch_all("SELECT ID, CUSTOMER, TOTAL FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?",
                              ["OPEN"], model=Order)
revenue = Query.fetch_val("SELECT SUM(TOTAL) FROM ORDERS WHERE STATUS = ?", ["PAID"])
daily = Query.fetch_polars("SELECT CAST(CREATED_AT AS DATE) AS ORDER_DAY, COUNT(*) AS N "
                           "FROM ORDERS GROUP BY 1")

results = pool.run_all([open_orders, revenue, daily], timeout=30.0)
results[open_orders]  # list[Order], typed by the Query
results[revenue]      # the value (fetch_val is typed Any)
results[daily]        # polars.DataFrame
```

Handle each result as soon as it finishes with `run_many`:

```python
with pool.run_many([open_orders, revenue, daily], concurrency=2) as group:
    for done in group:  # completion order
        print(done.index, done.query.sql, done.result())
```

And in async code:

```python
results = await pool.run_all_async([open_orders, revenue, daily])

async with pool.run_many_async(queries) as group:
    async for done in group:
        handle(done.query, done.result())
```

- Factories: `Query.fetch_all`, `fetch_one`, `fetch_val`, `fetch_json`,
  `fetch_arrow`, `fetch_polars`, `explain`. Streams are not available in groups.
- Each `Query` object is a distinct key; create two objects to run the same SQL
  twice. Passing the same object twice raises `ArgumentError`.
- `fail_fast=True` (default) cancels the rest on the first error and raises it;
  `fail_fast=False` runs everything and collects failures in `results.errors`.
- `timeout=` is a deadline for the whole group and cancels what is unfinished;
  each `Query` keeps its own `timeout=`. Leaving a `run_many` block cancels
  unfinished queries.
- Prefer `run_all_async` over `asyncio.gather` of many `*_async` calls: a plain
  `gather` of more than `pool_size + max_waiters` (264 by default) calls fails
  with `PoolBusyError`.
- Groups run on the pool, not inside a snapshot. Each query uses its own
  transaction, so the results are not a consistent snapshot of each other.

## See also

- [Errors](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/errors.md) and [troubleshooting](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md)
- [Configuration](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/configuration.md), [performance](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/performance.md) and the
  [API reference](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/api.md)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/errors.md -->

# Errors

Every error raised by fbfast derives from `fbfast.FbFastError`. The classes are
defined in [`python/fbfast/_errors.py`](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/python/fbfast/_errors.py)
and exported from the `fbfast` namespace. Some also derive from a built-in
exception, so generic handlers keep working:

- `QueryTimeoutError` and `PoolTimeoutError` are also `TimeoutError`.
- `DatabaseConnectionError` is also `ConnectionError`.
- `UsageError` is also `RuntimeError`; `ArgumentError` is also `ValueError` and `TypeError`.

Two errors that are **not** `FbFastError` can reach you from fbfast calls:
`pydantic.ValidationError` when a row does not fit your `model=` (rows are never
skipped silently), and `ImportError` when an optional extra (`pydantic`, `arrow`,
`polars`) is not installed.

## Hierarchy

```text
FbFastError
├── ConfigurationError
├── UnsupportedFeatureError
├── UnsupportedStatementError
├── ReadOnlyViolationError
├── ClientLibraryError
├── UsageError                 (also RuntimeError)
├── ArgumentError              (also ValueError, TypeError)
├── PoolError
│   ├── ForkSafetyError
│   ├── PoolClosedError
│   ├── PoolBusyError
│   │   └── ConcurrentUseError
│   ├── PoolTimeoutError       (also TimeoutError)
│   ├── PoolNotInitializedError
│   └── PoolAlreadyInitializedError
├── QueryCancelledError
├── QueryError
│   ├── QueryTimeoutError      (also TimeoutError)
│   └── DatabaseConnectionError (also ConnectionError)
├── AuthenticationError
├── RoleNotActiveError
├── UnsupportedServerError
├── DataConversionError
├── UnsupportedTypeError
├── ResultLimitError
└── CleanupError
```

## Reference

"Retry?" answers one question: can running the same call again, unchanged,
succeed? fbfast itself never repeats SQL that already reached the server.

| Exception | Base classes | Typical `phase` | When it happens | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ConfigurationError` | `FbFastError` | `config`, `registry` | Missing, invalid or unknown `FirebirdConfig` option, unreadable `.env`, empty pool name. | No. Fix the configuration. |
| `UnsupportedFeatureError` | `FbFastError` | `config` | `read_only=False`, or a connection charset other than UTF8. | No. |
| `UnsupportedStatementError` | `FbFastError` | `validate` | The SQL is not a single read-only `SELECT`/`WITH` query (DML, DDL, `EXECUTE BLOCK`, `WITH LOCK`, several statements). Nothing was sent to the server. | No. |
| `ReadOnlyViolationError` | `FbFastError` | `validate`, `attach` | A write was detected, or the session handshake did not confirm a READ ONLY transaction. | No. |
| `ClientLibraryError` | `FbFastError` | `load_client` | The Firebird client library could not be loaded or is older than 5.0.3. | No. Reinstall the wheel or fix `client_library`. |
| `UsageError` | `FbFastError`, `RuntimeError` | `python` | API misuse: querying a snapshot or stream outside its `with` block, entering one twice, `concurrency=0` in `run_all`. | No. Fix the code. |
| `ArgumentError` | `FbFastError`, `ValueError`, `TypeError` | `python` | Invalid argument: `model=` that is not a Pydantic v2 model, a non-`Query` in `run_all`, the same `Query` object twice, `unsupported=` other than `"error"`/`"string"`. | No. |
| `ForkSafetyError` | `PoolError` | `lifecycle`, `registry`, `async_runtime` | A pool, snapshot or stream created before `fork()` was used in the child. | No. Create pools after forking. |
| `PoolClosedError` | `PoolError` | `acquire`, `snapshot`, `stream`, `worker` | The pool is closing or closed; a snapshot already ended (any error ends it). | No. Use a new pool or a new snapshot. |
| `PoolBusyError` | `PoolError` | `acquire`, `delivery` | The waiting queue is full (`max_waiters`), or more async calls are pending than `pool_size + max_waiters`. | Yes, after a pause. For many queries use `run_all_async`. |
| `ConcurrentUseError` | `PoolBusyError` | `snapshot`, `stream` | A snapshot or stream was used by two operations at once (for example a query while a stream from the same snapshot is open). | No. Serialize the use. |
| `PoolTimeoutError` | `PoolError`, `TimeoutError` | `acquire`, `attach`, `close` | No connection became ready within `acquire_timeout` (or `connect_timeout` for opening one); closing did not finish within `close_timeout`. | Yes, later. Check pool size and the server. |
| `PoolNotInitializedError` | `PoolError` | `registry` | `get_pool(name)` found no ready pool (never initialized, still opening or closing). | No. Call `init_pool` first. |
| `PoolAlreadyInitializedError` | `PoolError` | `registry` | `init_pool(name=...)` with a name that is registered, opening or draining. | No. |
| `QueryCancelledError` | `FbFastError` | `query`, `stream`, `delivery` | The operation was cancelled: its stream was closed, its group was cancelled or the pool shut down. | Only if the cancellation was not intended. |
| `QueryError` | `FbFastError` | `prepare`, `execute`, `fetch`, ... | Firebird rejected or failed the statement (unknown column, missing privilege, arithmetic overflow...). Inspect `sqlstate` and `native_codes`. | Usually no. |
| `QueryTimeoutError` | `QueryError`, `TimeoutError` | `query`, `fetch`, `snapshot`, `group`, `stream_idle` | The deadline expired: `query_timeout` or `timeout=`, the snapshot deadline, a group `timeout=`, or `stream_idle_timeout`. | Only with a longer deadline or a cheaper query. |
| `DatabaseConnectionError` | `QueryError`, `ConnectionError` | `attach`, any (SQLSTATE `08xxx`) | The connection could not be opened or was lost. A failure before any SQL is sent is already retried once inside `acquire_timeout`. | Yes. A plain `SELECT` is idempotent; fbfast did not repeat it. |
| `AuthenticationError` | `FbFastError` | `attach` | SQLSTATE `28000`: wrong user or password, or incompatible wire encryption (`native_codes` contains `335545064`). | No. |
| `RoleNotActiveError` | `FbFastError` | `attach` | `role=` is not active for the session: wrong name or no `GRANT role TO user`. | No. |
| `UnsupportedServerError` | `FbFastError` | `attach` | The server is not Firebird 5.0.x. | No. |
| `DataConversionError` | `FbFastError` | `bind`, `describe`, `decode`, `python_conversion`, `polars` | A value cannot be converted exactly; wrong number or type of parameters; duplicate column names where names are keys (dicts, models, JSON records, Arrow); invalid bytes for `fallback_charset`. | No. |
| `UnsupportedTypeError` | `FbFastError` | `describe`, `decode` | A column or parameter type fbfast does not convert (ARRAY), or Decimal256 in `fetch_polars` without `unsupported="string"`. | No. |
| `ResultLimitError` | `FbFastError` | `materialize`, `read_blob` | A materialized result exceeded `max_result_bytes` or `max_result_rows`, or one BLOB exceeded `max_blob_bytes`. | No. Stream, filter, or raise the limit. |
| `CleanupError` | `FbFastError` | `cleanup`, `close` | Closing a cursor, transaction, statement or connection failed; the connection was discarded. | The pool keeps working; see below. |

`PoolError` is the base of the pool classes and is never raised by itself;
`FbFastError` is the catch-all.

## Reading an error

Every instance carries four attributes, also on errors raised in Python:

| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phase` | `str` | Where it failed. `"python"` for checks made in Python, `"config"` for configuration, `"attach"` for opening a connection, `"acquire"` for waiting on the pool, `"validate"` for the SQL checks done before anything is sent, `"prepare"`/`"bind"`/`"execute"`/`"fetch"` for the statement, `"query"`/`"snapshot"`/`"group"` for deadlines, `"cleanup"`/`"close"` for releasing resources. |
| `sqlstate` | `str \| None` | Five-character SQLSTATE reported by Firebird, such as `42S22` (unknown column), `28000` (authentication) or `08006` (connection failure). `None` when the error did not come from the server. |
| `native_codes` | `list[int]` | The Firebird status vector (`isc_*` codes), outermost first. Search them in the Firebird error-code list when the message is not enough. |
| `cleanup_errors` | `list[BaseException]` | Secondary failures that happened while cleaning up after this error. The original error is kept; each secondary failure is also added to the traceback with `add_note()`. |

```python
import fbfast

try:
    pool.fetch_all("SELECT NO_SUCH_COLUMN FROM RDB$DATABASE")
except fbfast.QueryError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__, error.phase, error.sqlstate, error.native_codes)
    # QueryError prepare 42S22 [335544569, 335544436, 335544578, 335544382, 336397208]
```

### Cleanup failures after the reply

Since 0.3.0 a pooled query returns as soon as its result is complete and its
cursor is closed. Rollback and `ALTER SESSION RESET` run afterwards, while the
connection stays unavailable to other callers ("deferred cleanup"). If that
cleanup fails, the connection is discarded and the failure is counted in
`pool.stats()["cleanup_errors"]`; the caller keeps its complete, valid result
and receives no `CleanupError`. `CleanupError` is still raised when cleanup is
part of the call you made: `pool.close()`, leaving a snapshot or a stream.

### Errors in query groups

With `run_all(..., fail_fast=True)` (the default) the first error cancels the
other queries and is raised from `run_all`. With `fail_fast=False`, every query
runs; `results.errors` maps each failed `Query` to its error and
`results[query]` raises it. In `run_many`, `done.result()` raises and
`done.exception()` returns the error. A group `timeout=` raises
`QueryTimeoutError` with `phase == "group"`.

## Retrying safely

Retry only errors that can succeed unchanged, and never retry
`ConcurrentUseError` even though it is a `PoolBusyError`:

```python
import time

import fbfast

RETRYABLE = (fbfast.DatabaseConnectionError, fbfast.PoolTimeoutError, fbfast.PoolBusyError)


def fetch_all_with_retry(pool: fbfast.Pool, sql: str, params=None, attempts: int = 3):
    for attempt in range(attempts):
        try:
            return pool.fetch_all(sql, params)
        except RETRYABLE as error:
            if isinstance(error, fbfast.ConcurrentUseError) or attempt == attempts - 1:
                raise
            time.sleep(0.2 * 2**attempt)
```

Rules of thumb:

- Before any SQL is sent, fbfast already replaces a broken idle connection once
  within `acquire_timeout` (counted in `stats()["reconnects"]`). After SQL was
  sent, the error is returned, never retried. Within `ready_transaction_timeout`
  (2 s) of a connection's previous query, the query itself is the first exchange,
  so a link that dropped meanwhile surfaces as `DatabaseConnectionError`.
- A `SELECT` from a selectable procedure can have side effects (generators are
  not rolled back). Retry those only if they are idempotent.
- Do not retry inside an open snapshot: any error ends it. Start a new one.
- When the session handshake finds a mismatch with your configuration
  (charset, time zone, wire-encryption policy), fbfast raises a plain
  `QueryError` with `phase == "attach"` and no `sqlstate`: retrying does not fix
  those. `DatabaseConnectionError` is reserved for failures the server or the
  network reported (SQLSTATE class 08, or a refused attach).

See [troubleshooting](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md) for specific messages and fixes.

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

Symptoms, causes and fixes for problems seen in practice. Each section names the
exception you get; [errors](https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/errors.md) explains the hierarchy and its attributes.

Two tools answer most questions without touching the server again:

```python
info = pool.session_info()   # negotiated capabilities of the latest connection, or None
stats = pool.stats()          # pool counters (no I/O)
traces = pool.diagnostics()   # per-query phases; needs FirebirdConfig(diagnostics=True)
```

`session_info()` returns `server_version`, `role`, `charset`, `time_zone`,
`wire_encrypted`, `wire_compressed`, `network_protocol`, `protocol_version`,
`inline_blobs`, `max_inline_blob_size` and `blob_cache_size`.

## Connecting

### `AuthenticationError`: "Incompatible wire encryption levels requested on client and server"

`wire_crypt` defaults to `"required"`. A server with `WireCrypt = Disabled`
refuses it, and a server with the default `WireCrypt = Required` refuses a
client configured with `"disabled"`. Firebird reports this with SQLSTATE
`28000`, so it arrives as `AuthenticationError`; `native_codes` contains
`335545064`.

- Prefer enabling encryption on the server and keeping `wire_crypt="required"`.
- `wire_crypt="enabled"` negotiates encryption but accepts an unencrypted
  connection. Use it, or `"disabled"`, only on a transport you trust (for
  example a WireGuard/Tailscale tunnel). Check `session_info()["wire_encrypted"]`.
- `QueryError` (phase `attach`) "Effective wire encryption violates the
  configured policy" means the negotiated result contradicts your setting; fix
  the configuration rather than retrying.

### `AuthenticationError` with "user name and password are not defined"

Wrong user or password, or the server's `AuthServer` list does not include
`Srp256`/`Srp`, which the bundled client uses. `Legacy_Auth` is not offered.

### `RoleNotActiveError`: "Requested role is not active"

The session did not end up with the role you asked for. Either the name is
wrong, or the user lacks `GRANT <role> TO <user>`. Unquoted role names are
compared in upper case; pass a quoted name (`role='"MixedCase"'`) only for a
role created with a quoted identifier. `session_info()["role"]` shows the active
role; with `role=None` it is `NONE`.

### `DatabaseConnectionError` at `attach`

SQLSTATE `08001`/`08006` and messages such as "Unable to complete network
request" or "I/O error during open" mean the server, port or database path is
wrong or unreachable. `database` is the alias or the path **on the server**.
fbfast only supports remote TCP connections (`network_protocol` `TCPv4`/`TCPv6`),
including to `localhost`; embedded and XNET connections are rejected.

When the session handshake finds that the connection differs from the
configuration (charset, time zone or encryption policy), the error is a plain
`QueryError` with phase `attach` and no `sqlstate`: retrying does not help.

### `UnsupportedServerError`, `ClientLibraryError`

fbfast talks to Firebird 5.0.x servers only. The wheels bundle the official
5.0.3 client; `ClientLibraryError` means that library (or the one set with
`client_library`) could not be loaded. Reinstall the wheel for your platform
and Python version instead of copying files between environments.

## Character sets and text

### `UnsupportedFeatureError`: the connection charset must be UTF8

Only UTF8 connections are supported (`charset="UTF8"`, the default). This does
not limit your columns: the server converts WIN1252, ISO8859_1 and other column
charsets to UTF8 on the way out, and you receive `str`.

### Text comes back as `bytes`

Columns and expressions with charset `NONE` (some legacy tables, and functions
such as `RDB$GET_CONTEXT`) have no declared encoding, so fbfast returns bytes.
Set `fallback_charset="UTF8"` to decode them, or `CAST(... AS VARCHAR(n)
CHARACTER SET UTF8)` in SQL. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 raise
`DataConversionError`.

### Trailing spaces in `CHAR` columns

`CHAR(n)` values keep their padding (system tables use `CHAR(63)` for names).
Use `TRIM()` in SQL or `trim_char=True`; `VARCHAR` is never trimmed.

## Parameters and columns

### `DataConversionError`: "Parameter 1 is incompatible with Firebird type 510"

Parameters are bound exactly; strings are not parsed into dates or numbers.
Pass the Python type that matches the SQL type:

| SQL type (code in the message) | Python value |
| --- | --- |
| `VARCHAR`/`CHAR` (448/452) | `str` |
| `SMALLINT`/`INTEGER`/`BIGINT`/`INT128` (500/496/580/32752) | `int` |
| `NUMERIC`/`DECIMAL` (stored as 500/496/580/32752 with a scale) | `decimal.Decimal` or `int` (a `float` is rejected) |
| `DOUBLE PRECISION`/`FLOAT` (480/482) | `float` (an `int` is rejected) |
| `DATE` (570) | `datetime.date` |
| `TIMESTAMP` (510) | `datetime.datetime` |
| `TIME` (560) | `datetime.time` |
| `BOOLEAN` (32764) | `bool` |

"Expected 1 parameters, received 0" means the number of `?` placeholders and
values differ. `params` must be a list, a tuple or `None`; one value is `[value]`.

### `DataConversionError`: "Duplicate column names; provide unique aliases"

Tuples allow repeated names, but dictionaries (`as_dict=True`), Pydantic models,
JSON with `orient="records"`, Arrow and Polars use column names as keys.
Give every column a unique alias: `SELECT O.ID, C.ID AS CUSTOMER_ID ...`.

### Pydantic: "Field required" for a column that is there

Firebird returns unquoted identifiers in UPPER CASE, so `SELECT id FROM ...`
produces the key `ID`. Name the fields in upper case, add
`Field(validation_alias="ID")`, or quote the alias in SQL (`AS "id"`). fbfast
does not rename columns.

### `UnsupportedTypeError`: "Polars cannot preserve Decimal256"

INT128-based values become Arrow Decimal256, and Polars cannot hold Decimal256.
In Firebird 4+ these appear more often than expected: `INT128` and
`NUMERIC(38, x)` columns, and also `SUM()` over `BIGINT` or `NUMERIC(18, x)`, and
`BIGINT * BIGINT`. Choose one:

- `CAST(SUM(TOTAL) AS NUMERIC(18, 2))` in SQL, when the value fits;
- `fetch_polars(..., unsupported="string")` to receive exact decimal text;
- `fetch_arrow(...)` (PyArrow keeps Decimal256), or `fetch_all` (Python `Decimal`).

## Slow queries over a WAN or tunnel

Start with `FirebirdConfig(diagnostics=True)`: each record of
`pool.diagnostics()` lists phases (`queue`, `begin`, `prepare`, `execute`,
`fetch`, `cleanup`...) with `seconds` and `roundtrips`. Round trips times your
latency is usually the whole story on a remote link.

- A cached query in a pool answers after 1 round trip (execute plus the first
  batch) when its connection has a transaction ready, and after 2 (begin,
  execute) otherwise. The session reset runs after the reply and starts that
  ready transaction; it is rolled back after `ready_transaction_timeout` (2 s)
  without use. `diagnostics` shows `begin` with 0 round trips when it was used.
- `DatabaseConnectionError` right after a network blip: if the link drops within
  `ready_transaction_timeout` of the previous query, the next query on that
  connection is the first exchange and may already have reached the server, so
  fbfast reports it instead of retrying. After that window, a dead connection is
  replaced before any SQL is sent. Set `ready_transaction_timeout=None` to always
  get the transparent replacement at the cost of one extra round trip.
- Many small queries in a row: put them in `pool.snapshot()`, about 1 round trip
  each, or run independent ones together with `run_all`.
- An idle connection is pinged after `health_check_after` seconds in the
  background, which also keeps tunnels and NAT mappings open.

### BLOB columns are slow

Firebird 5.0.3+ sends BLOBs up to `max_inline_blob_size` (65535 bytes by
default) inside the row. Without that, every BLOB value costs extra round trips.
fbfast 0.2.1 lost the inline path for text BLOBs; at 20 ms of latency, 1,000 rows
with a small text BLOB took 24 s with 0.2.1 and 0.19 s with 0.3.0.

1. Check `session_info()["inline_blobs"]`. It is `False` before server 5.0.3
   (protocol 19) or with `max_inline_blob_size=0`. Upgrade the server; prefer
   5.0.4 or later, because 5.0.3 keeps memory for each inline BLOB until the
   transaction ends.
2. UTF8, ISO8859_1, NONE, OCTETS and binary BLOBs are read inline. Text BLOBs in
   other charsets (WIN1252, for example) still go through the server's
   conversion filter, one extra round trip per value. Convert those columns, or
   `CAST` them in SQL.
3. Values larger than the inline limit are always read separately.
4. `CAST` short text to the smallest `VARCHAR` that fits, never `VARCHAR(8191)`
   by habit: wide rows mean fewer rows per round trip. `LIST()` returns a BLOB.
5. Compare `roundtrips` in `diagnostics()` with and without the BLOB column.

### Wire compression is not negotiated

`wire_compression=True` only asks; check `session_info()["wire_compressed"]`.
Both sides need zlib: Linux wheels use the system `libz.so.1` (install zlib if
it is missing), Windows wheels bundle `zlib1.dll`, and macOS wheels bundle a
small shim that loads the system zlib (the official macOS client looked for a
library name no macOS provides, so compression never worked there before 0.3.0).
If the client side is fine, the server lacks zlib. Compression helps on slow or
metered links and costs CPU on a fast LAN.

## Pools, snapshots and concurrency

### `PoolBusyError` versus `ConcurrentUseError`

| | `PoolBusyError` | `ConcurrentUseError` (a subclass) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cause | Too many callers: the waiting queue (`max_waiters`) is full, or more than `pool_size + max_waiters` async calls are pending. | One snapshot or stream used by two operations at once, e.g. a query while a stream from the same snapshot is open. |
| Fix | Back off and retry, raise `max_waiters`, or use `run_all`/`run_all_async` for batches, which never overflow the queue. | Serialize the use. Finish or close the stream first; never share a snapshot between threads or tasks. Retrying does not help. |

Catch `ConcurrentUseError` before `PoolBusyError` if you handle both.

### `PoolTimeoutError` while acquiring

No connection became ready within `acquire_timeout` (5 s). Either all
`pool_size` connections were busy (`stats()["leased"]`, `stats()["waiting"]`)
or opening a new one was slow or failing. Raise `pool_size`, shorten long
queries, or check the network.

### Which timeout fired?

| Setting | Default | Covers | Error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `acquire_timeout` | 5 s | Waiting for a ready connection, including opening one. | `PoolTimeoutError`, phase `acquire` |
| `connect_timeout` | 5 s | Attach and handshake of one connection (also bounded by `acquire_timeout`). | `PoolTimeoutError`, phase `attach` |
| `query_timeout` / `timeout=` | 30 s | One query, including fetching, conversion and consuming a stream. `None` disables it. | `QueryTimeoutError`, phase `query` or `fetch` |
| `snapshot_timeout` / `snapshot(timeout=)` | 300 s | The whole snapshot scope, including your code between queries. | `QueryTimeoutError`, phase `snapshot` |
| `run_all(timeout=)` | none | A whole query group; unfinished queries are cancelled. | `QueryTimeoutError`, phase `group` |
| `stream_idle_timeout` | 30 s | A stream waiting for its consumer to ask for more. | `QueryTimeoutError`, phase `stream_idle` |
| `close_timeout` | 10 s | Closing the pool, a snapshot or a stream. | `PoolTimeoutError` |
| `lock_timeout` | 5 s | Server-side lock waits. | `QueryError` |

Inside a snapshot each query uses the smaller of its own deadline and what is
left of the snapshot's. Passing `timeout=None` to a query does not disable the
snapshot deadline.

### Errors inside a snapshot

Any error ends a snapshot. Later calls on it, and leaving its `with` block,
raise that error again; catch it outside the block and open a new snapshot.
Using a snapshot or stream outside its `with` block raises `UsageError`.

### `TypeError: 'NoneType' object can't be awaited` after upgrading

0.3.0 renamed the lifecycle methods: no suffix blocks, `_async` (and `aclose`)
is a coroutine.

| Up to 0.2.x | 0.3.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `pool.close_sync()` / `await pool.close()` | `pool.close()` / `await pool.aclose()` |
| `pool.warmup_sync()` / `await pool.warmup()` | `pool.warmup()` / `await pool.warmup_async()` |
| `pool.clear_statement_cache_sync()` / `await pool.clear_statement_cache()` | `pool.clear_statement_cache()` / `await pool.clear_statement_cache_async()` |
| `snapshot.close_sync()` / `await snapshot.close()` | `snapshot.close()` / `await snapshot.aclose()` |
| `init_pool_sync()` / `await init_pool()` | `init_pool()` / `await init_pool_async()` |
| `close_pool_sync()` / `await close_pool()` | `close_pool()` / `await close_pool_async()` |
| `async with pool.snapshot_async()` | `async with pool.snapshot()` |

The old `_sync` names and `snapshot_async()` still work with a
`DeprecationWarning` until 0.4.0. Names whose meaning flipped have no alias:
`await pool.close()` now closes the pool synchronously and then fails with
`TypeError`, so old code fails loudly instead of leaking connections.

### `ForkSafetyError` and worker processes

Pools, snapshots and streams belong to the process that created them. Using
one in a child after `fork()` raises `ForkSafetyError`, and named pools
registered before the fork are rejected the same way.

- Importing fbfast before forking is fine; create pools in each worker after it
  starts (FastAPI lifespan, Gunicorn `post_fork`, Celery `worker_process_init`).
- Do not open a pool at import time in an app loaded with `--preload`.
- If the parent process has already used fbfast, start workers with the
  `spawn` start method (`multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`). A child forked
  from such a process should not create a new pool either.

### Statement errors after a schema change

Prepared statements are cached per connection. After DDL changes a table,
drain active work and call `pool.clear_statement_cache()` (or
`await pool.clear_statement_cache_async()`), or recreate the pool.

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/rafael-peter/fbfast/blob/v0.3.0/docs/guide/configuration.md -->

# Configuration

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_docs.py from python/fbfast/_native.pyi; do not edit. -->

`FirebirdConfig()` resolves every option from, in order: the explicit keyword
argument, the `FB_<NAME>` environment variable, the same variable in a `.env`
file in the current directory, and the default below. `database`, `user` and
`password` are required. Construction validates all values and never connects.

```python
import fbfast

config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig()                      # FB_* variables and .env
config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig(pool_size=4, query_timeout=10.0, env_file=False)
config = fbfast.FirebirdConfig.from_env("FB_BI_")     # FB_BI_HOST, FB_BI_DATABASE...
```

In the environment and `.env`, numbers are text, booleans accept
`true/false`, `1/0` and `yes/no`, and `none` means `None`. Durations are
seconds. An explicit `None` wins over the environment for options that accept
it. Unknown options and invalid values raise `ConfigurationError`.

| Option | Environment | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | `FB_HOST` | `"localhost"` | Firebird server host name or address (non-empty str). |
| `port` | `FB_PORT` | `3050` | TCP port (int, 1..65535). |
| `database` | `FB_DATABASE` | `required` | Database alias or path on the server (non-empty str). |
| `user` | `FB_USER` | `required` | Firebird user (non-empty str). |
| `password` | `FB_PASSWORD` | `required` | Password (non-empty str), hidden in repr. Accessing config.password returns a normal str; never log it. |
| `role` | `FB_ROLE` | `None` | SQL role to activate (str \| None). An explicit None ignores a role from the environment. |
| `read_only` | `FB_READ_ONLY` | `True` | Only True is supported (Literal[True]); False raises UnsupportedFeatureError. |
| `charset` | `FB_CHARSET` | `"UTF8"` | Connection charset (non-empty str). Only UTF8 is supported by the executor. |
| `session_time_zone` | `FB_SESSION_TIME_ZONE` | `"UTC"` | Session time zone such as "America/Sao_Paulo" (non-empty str). |
| `client_library` | `FB_CLIENT_LIBRARY` | `None` | Path to a libfbclient to use instead of the bundled one (str \| None). |
| `wire_crypt` | `FB_WIRE_CRYPT` | `"required"` | Wire encryption policy: "required", "enabled" or "disabled"; bools are accepted (True=required, False=disabled). "enabled" allows an unencrypted connection; keep "required" unless the transport is reviewed. |
| `wire_compression` | `FB_WIRE_COMPRESSION` | `False` | Request zlib wire compression; the server must agree. Helps on slow links, costs CPU on fast ones. Check Pool.session_info()["wire_compressed"]. |
| `app_name` | `FB_APP_NAME` | `"fbfast"` | Application name reported to the server (non-empty str). |
| `pool_size` | `FB_POOL_SIZE` | `8` | Maximum connections and native workers (int >= 1); must be >= min_idle. Also the default and maximum concurrency of run_all/run_many. |
| `min_idle` | `FB_MIN_IDLE` | `2` | Connections kept open and ready (0 <= int <= pool_size). Use 0 to keep none. |
| `max_waiters` | `FB_MAX_WAITERS` | `256` | Calls allowed to wait in the queue (int >= 1); a full queue raises PoolBusyError. |
| `acquire_timeout` | `FB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` | `5.0` | Seconds to obtain a ready connection, including any attach/handshake (float; None not allowed). |
| `connect_timeout` | `FB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | `5.0` | Seconds for attach and handshake, also bounded by acquire_timeout (float). |
| `idle_timeout` | `FB_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `300.0` | Seconds idle before connections beyond min_idle are closed (float). |
| `max_lifetime` | `FB_MAX_LIFETIME` | `1800.0` | Target connection lifetime in seconds, jittered so recycling spreads out; active work is never interrupted (float). |
| `health_check_after` | `FB_HEALTH_CHECK_AFTER` | `30.0` | Seconds idle after which a connection is pinged; done off the critical path, which also keeps tunnels and NAT mappings alive (float). |
| `close_timeout` | `FB_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` | `10.0` | Seconds to wait for close/cleanup (float). Native work still pending after it stays counted until it finishes. |
| `fetch_size` | `FB_FETCH_SIZE` | `5000` | Target rows per batch (int >= 1); also the default batch_rows of streams. |
| `batch_bytes` | `FB_BATCH_BYTES` | `4_194_304 (4 MiB)` | Byte budget per batch (int >= 1); a single larger row forms its own batch. BLOB batches close once their decoded bytes reach it. Not a limit on total Python memory. |
| `prefetch_batches` | `FB_PREFETCH_BATCHES` | `1` | Batches fetched ahead of the consumer (int >= 0); zero disables read-ahead. |
| `max_result_bytes` | `FB_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` | `536_870_912 (512 MiB)` | Cumulative budget per materialized result (int >= 1 \| None); does not apply to streams and is not an exact RSS cap. None disables it. |
| `max_result_rows` | `FB_MAX_RESULT_ROWS` | `None` | Row limit per materialized result (int >= 1 \| None); does not apply to streams. |
| `max_blob_bytes` | `FB_MAX_BLOB_BYTES` | `67_108_864 (64 MiB)` | Limit per BLOB value, also in streams (int >= 1). Known text charsets count bytes after conversion to UTF-8; exceeding it raises ResultLimitError. |
| `query_timeout` | `FB_QUERY_TIMEOUT` | `30.0` | Default per-query deadline in seconds, including fetching and Python conversion (float \| None). None disables it. |
| `lock_timeout` | `FB_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | `5` | Seconds the server waits for locks (int >= 0); zero means NO WAIT. |
| `stream_idle_timeout` | `FB_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `30.0` | Seconds a stream producer waits for the consumer to ask for more (float \| None); None disables it. Independent of query_timeout. |
| `statement_cache_size` | `FB_STATEMENT_CACHE_SIZE` | `64` | Prepared statements kept per connection (int >= 0); zero disables the cache. |
| `statement_cache_bytes` | `FB_STATEMENT_CACHE_BYTES` | `8_388_608 (8 MiB)` | Estimated statement cache budget per connection (int >= 1, bytes). |
| `trim_char` | `FB_TRIM_CHAR` | `False` | Strip trailing spaces from CHAR columns, never VARCHAR (bool). |
| `fallback_charset` | `FB_FALLBACK_CHARSET` | `None` | Charset for text without one (charset NONE), str \| None. Currently only UTF8/UTF-8; applies to text and NONE text BLOBs. Invalid bytes raise DataConversionError. |
| `snapshot_timeout` | `FB_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT` | `300.0` | Deadline for a whole snapshot scope, including time between its queries (float \| None, seconds). Each query inside still uses query_timeout. None disables it. |
| `max_inline_blob_size` | `FB_MAX_INLINE_BLOB_SIZE` | `None` | Largest BLOB a Firebird 5.0.3+ server sends together with its row (int 0..65535 \| None, bytes); 0 disables inline BLOBs. None keeps the client default (65535). |
| `blob_cache_size` | `FB_BLOB_CACHE_SIZE` | `None` | Client cache for inline BLOBs per connection (int >= 0 \| None, bytes). None keeps the client default (10 MiB). |
| `diagnostics` | `FB_DIAGNOSTICS` | `False` | Record time and round trips per phase for every pool query, read with Pool.diagnostics() (bool). Reading the counters adds no round trip. |
| `ready_transaction_timeout` | `FB_READY_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT` | `2.0` | After a query that read all its rows, its session reset also starts the next query's transaction, so the next query skips one round trip; an unused transaction is rolled back after this many idle seconds (float \| None). None disables the reuse. |

`env_file`: path of a dotenv file (str) or `False` to skip it. Omitted: read
`.env` in the current directory if it exists. There is no `FB_ENV_FILE`.
